cues: August Strindberg was Sweden's great dramatist, author of more than sixty plays.
In Miss Julie and The Father he brought naturalism to the stage: characters who speak and behave as in real life, driven by psychology and circumstance, not melodrama.
Later he wrote dream like plays that led towards expressionism.
He lived by Lake Geneva in the eighteen eighties, and that is where this play is set.
